gen-dafont-electroharmonix-lora: Electroharmonix splits each word into separate letters with open gaps, and its round characters swing wide and open-handed. Lora sits at a modest size, its curves thinning only mildly.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads with a prominent x-height, each curve swelling faintly like pulled taffy. And what stands out most is Electroharmonix, whose open gaps split every word into single letters.
gen-dafont-eraser-author: Author reads dignified and refined, with thin strokes free of hairlines beside moderately weighty stems. And pages of it pick up a slight swell on the bowls, while Eraser stays blunt and monoline above.
gen-dafont-eraser-fs-bespoke-slab: Eraser lays down bold letters with no thicker or thinner strokes, understated and commanding. And where Eraser hits hardest in a few big words, Bespoke Slab settles in with tall, refined lowercase.
gen-dafont-eraser-fs-paquito: Paquito reads confident and approachable, its lowercase standing almost as tall as its capitals. And with Eraser's joins staying full where strokes meet, extended text in Paquito keeps a sturdy, friendly pace.

gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-archivo: Espresso Dolce writes in neon-tube lines, a calligraphic hand with a wide-eyed lowercase e, every stroke traceable by finger. Archivo, a sans with a commanding x-height, keeps reading steady.
gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-fs-asap: Asap is a sans with c forms like open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals. Asap sits against Espresso Dolce's thread-stitched script, and that jump in lowercase height is the pair's real hook.
